detail.abstract: This paper introduces two original conceptual contributions to the literature on luxury consumption and structural economic transformation. The first, the Wealth Foundation Theory, argues that every luxury persona in history has been structurally determined by the mass economic base beneath it — from the seigneurial system of pre-revolutionary Europe to the welfare-state-created aspirational middle class of the late twentieth century. The second, the Legitimacy Fracture, identifies a growing and structurally irresolvable incoherence between the ethical positioning of contemporary luxury maisons and the increasingly illegitimate or fiscally optimized nature of the wealth that now sustains their revenues. Building on the Luxury Waterloo hypothesis (Korotkov, 2025a) and its strategic extensions (Korotkov, 2025b), this paper argues that post-WWII progressive taxation was the primary structural engine of luxury democratization — not brand strategy. The creation of a prosperous Western middle class through fiscal redistribution generated the aspirational consumer base that luxury brands subsequently courted from the 1990s onward. The Asian luxury consumer, whose emergence between 2000 and 2019 dramatically expanded the global luxury pyramid, is identified as a derivative phenomenon: wealth built on manufacturing revenues generated by Western middle-class consumption. The COVID-19 pandemic triggered a violent inversion of this wealth transfer, weakening the Western middle class while temporarily enriching Asian producers — setting in motion the mutual cannibalization of the two consumer bases that had jointly sustained luxury expansion. The paper presents a historical typology of six luxury personas, each structurally explained by its economic and fiscal conditions of production, anchored in practitioner field observations conducted in Cannes and Monte-Carlo between February 2025 and May 2026. Three forward scenarios for the luxury persona through 2030 are examined, and the strategic implications of the Legitimacy Fracture for luxury maisons are assessed.

detail.abstract: Recent work on hybrid Reinforcement Learning-Large Language Model (RL-LLM) trading agents, notably FinRL-DeepSeek [Benhenda, 2025], has revealed a counterintuitive empirical finding: increasing LLM signal infusion strength systematically degrades agent performance, even at perturbation magnitudes as small as 0.1%. We hypothesize that a key factor in this degradation is the absence of epistemic uncertainty estimation on LLM outputs: the agent has no mechanism to distinguish a high-confidence financial signal from an unreliable hallucination. Drawing inspiration from Monte Carlo Dropout techniques in medical imaging uncertainty quantification [Gal and Ghahramani, 2016], we propose UG-CPPO (Uncertainty-Gated CVaR-PPO), a novel architecture that dynamically gates LLM signal infusion based on prompt-ensemble-derived uncertainty. We query the LLM with N =5 semantically diverse prompts per news article and compute the standard deviation σ across responses; when σ exceeds a threshold τ , the gate closes and the signal is suppressed. We apply this gating mechanism to both the action modifier S f (PPO action perturbation) and the risk modifier R f (CVaR penalty). We evaluate the framework on the FNSPID dataset [Dong et al., 2024] with 28,502 (ticker, date) signals computed via OpenAI gpt-4o-mini, using 10seed evaluation on Nasdaq trading 2019-2023. The gating mechanism achieves the predicted activation rate (34.2% ± 0%, exactly within target [30-40%]) and we demonstrate that LLM uncertainty σ is structurally higher in bear markets (2022: 0.614) than in bull periods (2019: 0.525). However, at our computeconstrained scale (500,000 training steps, 10 stocks), UG-CPPO does not show statistically significant performance improvement over baselines on aggregate metrics (Wilcoxon p > 0.05): cumulative return 36.0% ± 38.7% versus 62.0% ± 37.6% for CPPO and 43.9% ± 32.2% for PPO. We document the methodology, release 30 trained agents and 55,360 LLM uncertainty signals, and identify training scale as the principal direction for future validation. Our contribution is a reusable uncertainty-gating mechanism with rigorous multi-seed empirical characterizationrare in this application domain.

detail.title: Oman's Snack Industry: Navigating Growth, Health, and Policy in a Dynamic Market
detail.abstract: This project analyzes the Omani snack food and chips industry from a microeconomic perspective, focusing on market structure, consumer behavior, price elasticity, supply challenges, and government policies. The study identifies the industry as operating under monopolistic competition, where local producers compete with international brands through product differentiation, pricing, and marketing strategies. Using secondary data from industry reports and academic sources, the research finds that the market is expected to grow from US$610 million in 2024 to US$878 million by 2030, driven by urbanization, changing lifestyles, and increasing demand for convenient and healthier snack options. At the same time, the industry faces major challenges, including heavy dependence on imports, rising production costs, and supply chain disruptions. The study also examines the impact of VAT, health regulations, and nutritional labeling policies on firms and consumers, highlighting the need to balance public health objectives with economic growth. The findings suggest that encouraging local production, supporting healthy snack innovation, and implementing balanced government policies are essential for achieving sustainable development and long-term competitiveness in Oman’s snack industry.

detail.abstract: This study examines the structural determinants of persistently high interest rate spreads and predatory lending practices in Sri Lanka's banking sector, a paradox wherein financial institutions report record profits while the productive economy, particularly small and medium enterprises (SMEs), faces systemic distress. Employing a Multivist philosophical framework within a qualitative comparative case study design, this research analyses two interrelated phenomena: the interest rate transmission mechanism from policy rates to lending rates, and the Parate Execution Law (Recovery of Loans by Banks Special Provisions Act No. 4 of 1990) as a legal mechanism enabling asset seizure without judicial oversight. Findings indicate that Sri Lanka's interest spread of 8-14 percentage points exceeds comparable economies by a factor of 2-3, representing a structural transfer of income from borrowers to financial institutions. The Parate Execution Law, which facilitated over 1,750 SME property auctions in 2023 alone, operates without independent valuation or court orders, a legal framework extraordinary in comparative perspective. The study contributes to financial intermediation theory by demonstrating how regulatory capture and legal coercion substitute for competitive discipline in concentrated banking markets. Policy implications include the need for spread regulation, judicial oversight of asset recovery, and development banking mechanisms for SME credit.

detail.abstract: We study a surgery scheduling problem under limited downstream ICU capacity, where the scheduling decisions are made before postoperative ICU demand is realized, while ICU admissions adapt to patient-specific feature information revealed after surgery. This temporal mismatch creates a misalignment between upstream surgical decisions and downstream ICU capacity, increasing congestion risk and operational inefficiency. To address this challenge, we develop a feature-driven robust optimization framework that integrates predictive modeling with operational decision-making. Our proposed model not only improves surgery-duration prediction but also preserves tractability and interpretability for optimization. Furthermore, to account for downstream congestion risk, we construct a feature-driven representation of ICU demand and formulate a distributionally robust capacity constraint. We show that this constraint can be equivalently transformed into a tractable Conditional Value-at-Risk measure, providing a risk-averse safeguard that effectively limits ICU congestion arising from adverse realizations of length-of-stay uncertainty and patient mix. Numerical studies using a comprehensive data set from a cardiology department in China demonstrate that our approach consistently outperforms traditional predict-then-optimize frameworks. In particular, our framework substantially reduces ICU bed shortages during peak-demand periods while improving operational robustness and enhancing the coordination between surgery scheduling and ICU capacity management.

title: Human Alignment Value and the Obsolescence of Man-Hours: A Computational Theory of Human Contribution in Human–AI Hybrid Organisations.

detail.title: Human Alignment Value and the Obsolescence of Man-Hours: A Computational Theory of Human Contribution in Human–AI Hybrid Organisations.
detail.abstract: The four preceding papers in this series established a computational theory of human–AI hybrid organisations: the multi-scale CPN–NK landscape architecture, the H+AI CM framework with token-budget governance, belief-misalignment pathology with the Q:F ratio, and process topology with IT:HR governance cost accounting. All four papers share a measurement assumption that has not been examined: human contribution is measured in man-hours. This paper examines that assumption and finds it structurally inadequate for organisations in which AI agents handle a structurally significant fraction of execution. We introduce Human Alignment Value (HAV) as the replacement unit. HAV is defined as the degree to which a human’s contribution cannot be reduced to a repeated endeavour — a fixed sequence of steps that an AI agent could execute with equal or superior fitness. HAV has three components: Non-Procedure Fraction (NPF), measuring time spent outside repeated-endeavour mode; SLA Recovery Quality (SRQ), measuring human performance at recovering AI agent failures that exceed SLO thresholds; and Origination Capacity (OC), measuring the rate at which a human generates new objective functions rather than optimising within existing ones. Man-hours conflates all three with zero-HAV repeated-endeavour execution time, producing systematic measurement error that worsens as AI autonomy increases. We formalise a four-mode human–AI spectrum (RPA, Assistant, Autonomous oversight, Fully Autonomous), derive the HAV crossover theorem — the AI autonomy threshold φ* at which HAV-governed organisations begin to outperform man-hours-governed organisations on NK fitness — and demonstrate computationally that organisations above φ* that continue to use man hours measurement actively incentivise Track 2 pathology. A dual-track model distinguishes profit from nonprofit organisations: the absence of a market correction mechanism in nonprofits makes values custodianship — the human capacity to maintain and reconstitute the founding belief — the most irreplaceable HAV-generating activity in the nonprofit sector, and the most systematically undervalued under man-hours accounting. The paper seeds the Paper 6 agenda on the Federation Marketplace: a prediction engine for HAV matching across organisational boundaries.

detail.abstract: Senate Bill 21 (SB 21) recast Delaware's law of controlling shareholder transactions, making it easier for controlling shareholders to obtain approval of related-party transactions. The reform has been controversial. This article argues that the central issue is not conflict of interest as such, but the opportunistic use of control discretion. SB 21 established procedures through which controllers may cleanse conflicts of interest, while leaving Delaware courts to police opportunistic compliance with those procedures. The broader lesson is that a European corporate law model, such as the EU Inc., requires a specialized EU court able to apply statutory rules uniformly and predictably while constraining their opportunistic use.

title: Adaptive Regional Piecewise Value Function Approximation: A Weighted, Error-Driven Fitted Value Iteration Approach
affiliations: , University of Ottawa and University of Ottawa

detail.title: Adaptive Regional Piecewise Value Function Approximation: A Weighted, Error-Driven Fitted Value Iteration Approach
detail.abstract: This paper addresses the inherent bias-variance limitations of approximate dynamic programming (ADP) in highdimensional stochastic control problems by introducing an Adaptive Piecewise Affine Approximate Optimal Policy (PW-AOP) through a novel Fitted Value Iteration algorithm. While traditional global affine approximations suffer from severe approximation bias when confronting non-linear system dynamics (e.g., congestion bottlenecks or threshold penalties), our method dynamically constructs a localized, separable piecewise affine value function. We depart from standard Monte Carlo trajectory evaluations by utilizing exact one-step look-ahead Bellman targets, effectively eliminating estimation variance caused by transition noise. Furthermore, the algorithm incorporates Dynamic State Relevance Weighting, which involves blending a strictly positive geometric prior with empirical policy visitation frequencies, to actively align the training distribution with the operational policy, thereby taming the concentrability coefficient. By evaluating Weighted Bellman Residuals (WBR), our approach automatically discovers and allocates partitioning breakpoints to regions of the state space exhibiting large WBRs due to critical non-linearities. We establish rigorous finite-time performance bounds for this methodology, proving that it systematically breaks the representational bottleneck of global affine architectures while strictly regulating the pseudo-dimension to prevent estimation error explosion. Across diverse and complex domains, including controllable queueing networks, battery management systems, and multi-priority patient scheduling, we conduct numerical experiments to demonstrate that our adaptive framework yields strictly superior control policies and tighter value function approximations, all while preserving the computational efficiency and structural interpretability of linear programming-based ADP.

detail.abstract:
Organizational Psychogenetics (OPG) is a theoretical framework addressing a question the existing organizational sciences have circled without resolving: what is the psychology of the organization itself, where does it come from, and what does it produce? Drawing on industrial-organizational psychology, systems psychodynamics, developmental psychology, psychoanalytic theory, and the epidemiology of adverse childhood experiences, this paper proposes three integrated claims. 

First, organizations have a psychology that is encoded from founding conditions. The founder's internal psychological organization generates relational schemas, narrative structures, and defensive patterns that are embedded in the organization before most of its current members arrive, and that persist across leadership succession and strategic reinvention. Second, organizational psychology is transmitted and inherited across generations of membership through identifiable mechanisms including the identified patient dynamic, leadership succession pathology, foreclosed territory, and narrative gaps. Third, because the workplace is the primary relational environment of adult life, this inherited psychology has measurable developmental consequences for the people who pass through it.

The paper introduces the concept of occupational reparenting to describe the process by which organizational membership reactivates early relational schemas and either confirms, disrupts, or deepens them. A genetic analogy structures the framework: founding psychology operates as an organizational genotype, while the observable behavioral and structural patterns it produces constitute the phenotype. Behavioral and structural interventions that do not reach the founding psychology leave the genotype intact, which the paper proposes as the primary explanation for the documented failure rate of organizational change initiatives. The paper closes with a research agenda for the field.

title: Drone Deployment for Blood Transport in India: A National Geospatial Simulation Study

detail.title: Drone Deployment for Blood Transport in India: A National Geospatial Simulation Study

detail.abstract:
Background: Timely access to blood products remains a major barrier to emergency care in low- and middle-income countries, particularly in rural and remote regions. In India—home to 23% of the global blood deficit—geographic disparities in blood availability compound national shortages, with nearly 40% of the rural population living over an hour from a blood bank. Drone-based delivery systems offer a potential means to improve equity and speed of access, yet their population-level impact has not been evaluated. 

Methods: We developed a national geospatial simulation model of drone-based blood delivery in India using data from the Ayushman Bharat Health Facility Registry, the Malaria Atlas Project motorized travel friction surface and WorldPop population data. First-referral units (FRUs) and blood banks were mapped, and simulated drone sites were placed at 1%, 5%, and 10% of blood banks, prioritized by population catchment impact. Travel times from blood banks to FRUs and total time to blood availability (TTBA) were calculated using Dijkstra’s algorithm. 

Findings: At baseline, 13% of rural FRUs and 38% of the rural population were over 60 minutes from a blood product. With 10% of blood banks as drone sites, the fraction of FRUs farther than 60 minutes fell to <2%. With drone deployment, 76 million people experience >30-minute reductions in TTBA.  

Interpretation: Strategically deployed drone networks could substantially reduce inequities in blood access across India. Geospatial modeling provides a framework for cost-effective, targeted drone deployment to improve emergency transfusion readiness in resource-limited settings.

title: Robust Corrective Policy under Joint Market and Government Failures: A Risk-Management Framework
affiliations: Tulane University

detail.title: Robust Corrective Policy under Joint Market and Government Failures: A Risk-Management Framework
detail.abstract: Public economists routinely invoke six canonical market failures to justify corrective government intervention. Yet the same discipline that identifies these failures also supplies a formidable array of theoretical constraints to such intervention that operate jointly and multiplicatively. This paper develops a microfounded recursive robust-control framework in which a policy planner confronts a known market failure f but faces deep uncertainty over a constraint vector θ that endogenously determines four success probabilities through explicit sub-models of political bargaining, regulatory signal extraction, bureaucratic persistence, and entrepreneurial discovery. Using Hansen-Sargent multiplier preferences with a distorted law of motion for discovery, the framework delivers a novel multiplicative-collapse threshold: the certainty-equivalent value of discretionary intervention is negative under baseline calibrations unless institutional quality raises the joint success probability above a precisely derived cutoff p(κ, dim(f)). This threshold and its comparative statics cannot be obtained from existing robust-control applications in public finance (which typically treat narrower forms of uncertainty) or from standalone political-economy models. The framework nests sufficient-statistics welfare analysis (Chetty, 2009) and mechanism-design results as special cases, supplies an operational calibration strategy linked to meta-analytic evidence, and generates sharp testable predictions on institutional design. Category-by-category applications show that only a narrow subclass of high-stakes negative externalities with strong commitment devices yields positive certainty-equivalent value.

title: The Boundary Within: Process Topology, Role Oscillation, and the Cost of Misalignment in Human-AI Hybrid Organisations

detail.title: The Boundary Within: Process Topology, Role Oscillation, and the Cost of Misalignment in Human-AI Hybrid Organisations
detail.abstract: Rajendra (2026a, 2026b, 2026c) established that belief-misalignment pathology is a structural failure mode in human-AI hybrid organisations whose two-stage contamination process degrades organisational fitness while internal quality metrics remain high. Those papers treat the organisational boundary as given. This paper introduces the boundary as a governance variable. Drawing on Coase (1937) and Williamson (1975, 1985) alongside the March-Simon-Cohen-March-Olsen tradition, we argue that the firm boundary in the human-AI context is a process topology question: the point in the BPMN process at which alignment governance is applied determines whether belief-misalignment can be detected and corrected at all. We formalise three BPMN topology conditions (flat, sequential gateway, parallel gateway), a role oscillation trichotomy (RPA, assistant, autonomous), a four-component cost model (compute, governance, misalignment opportunity cost, and Stage-2 remediation), and the IT:HR ratio as a governance architecture diagnostic. A central theoretical contribution is the identification of beliefmisalignment pathology as a third governance ontology distinct from both the self-interested agent assumed by Coase-Williamson transaction cost economics and the boundedly rational agent assumed by March-Simon organisational theory. AI agents are neither opportunistic nor cognitively limited in the relevant senses; their governance problem is architectural rather than behavioural or cognitive, and existing governance instruments calibrated to the first two ontologies cannot detect or correct it. Four propositions are derived and tested against 30-seed Monte Carlo experiments across three topology conditions, three role modes, and three landscape ruggedness levels. All four propositions are supported. The central finding is that governance architecturetopology, role mode, reviewer quality, and probe frequency-is a first-class design variable whose cost consequences are quantifiable, and that unified IT+HR governance consistently outperforms either attribution architecture alone because it implements a two-stage alignment filter that LLM-only evaluation cannot replicate.

title: The Garbage Can Cannot See Itself: Belief-Misalignment Pathology in Human-AI Hybrid Organisations

detail.title: The Garbage Can Cannot See Itself: Belief-Misalignment Pathology in Human-AI Hybrid Organisations
detail.abstract: Recent empirical work establishes that human-designed organisations are absorbing AI agents at unusually high failure rates. The MIT NANDA report finds that 95% of enterprise generative AI pilots produce no measurable P&L impact (Challapally et al., 2025). The Berkeley MAST taxonomy, derived from 1,642 multi-agent execution traces, identifies fourteen distinct failure modes clustered around specification, coordination, and verification (Cemri et al., 2025). Both findings converge on the conclusion that the failure mechanism is organisational rather than purely technical. Both prescribe technical fixes. This paper argues that the technical prescription is necessary but not sufficient. The deeper mechanism is belief-misalignment, a pathology that operates at three coupled levels of organisational existence: the AI agent's belief about its task domain (corpus-vs-reality), the human participant's belief about their role and contribution (participatory misalignment), and the organisation's founding belief about its reason for being (constitutive misalignment). The present paper formalises the AI-side track within a Coloured Petri Net implementation extending Rajendra (2026a, 2026b), introduces the quality-to-fitness (Q:F) ratio as the primary observable diagnostic, and demonstrates the two-stage contamination structure: Stage 1 produces a sustained alignment gap between solution quality and solution-framing fit, and Stage 2 manifests as measurable movement of the macro-belief template toward the AI agents' offset belief region. Thirty-seed Monte Carlo experiments demonstrate that template movement under sustained beliefdomain offset is a strong, robust effect (Cohen's d > 2.5 across offset conditions vs aligned baseline). The pathology is structurally invisible to internal AI observability and detectable only through measurement that crosses the boundary between AI observability and external operational fitness. Three detection heuristics are developed for the AI-side track. The cost-of-misalignment, process-topology, and role-oscillation governance design questions are deferred to Rajendra (2026d).

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning Framework for Diversified Portfolio Management Across Global Equity Markets

detail.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning Framework for Diversified Portfolio Management Across Global Equity Markets
detail.abstract: This study develops and evaluates a deep reinforcement learning framework for dynamic portfolio allocation across global equity markets. The Soft Actor-Critic algorithm is used to learn continuous portfolio weights within a Markov Decision Process, incorporating transaction costs, turnover penalties, and diversification constraints into the reward function. Five model configurations are compared, varying in reward formulation, policy structure (flat versus hierarchical Dirichlet), portfolio constraints, and temporal encoder (LSTM versus Transformer), and evaluated via walkforward optimization across sixteen out-of-sample folds spanning 2003-2026 on the Nasdaq-100, Nikkei 225, and Euro Stoxx 50. Results show that RL strategies achieve competitive risk-adjusted performance primarily in the Euro Stoxx 50, where statistically significant abnormal returns are observed, but the central hypothesis is only partially confirmed: no strategy achieves statistically significant excess returns relative to Buy & Hold under HAC-robust inference across all markets. Regime analysis reveals that RL adds the most value during periods of elevated uncertainty, while ensemble aggregation across markets improves risk-adjusted performance and confirms the benefits of geographic diversification.

title: Social Media Strategies for Building Trust in Nonprofit Hospitals a Conceptual Framework

detail.title: Social Media Strategies for Building Trust in Nonprofit Hospitals a Conceptual Framework
detail.abstract: The paper examines how nonprofit hospitals can use social media in health awareness campaigns to improve public engagement and build trust. The study responds to a gap in management and marketing research, where outcomes such as credibility and institutional trust are underexplored compared with awareness and behavioral measures. Findings: The review highlights three mechanisms: interactive communication increases engagement, transparent messaging strengthens credibility, and effective misinformation management protects trust. Together, these mechanisms suggest that social media can operate as more than an information channel, functioning as a relationship-building tool for nonprofit healthcare organizations. Theoretical Implications: The framework extends relationship marketing theory to the nonprofit hospital context, emphasizing engagement and trust as central outcomes of digital communication. Practical Implications: The paper provides hospital managers with guidelines for designing campaigns that prioritize transparency, interactivity, and community dialogue, offering a path to improve both health outcomes and institutional legitimacy. Originality/Value: By integrating insights from marketing, healthcare management, and nonprofit studies, the paper reframes social media use in nonprofit hospitals as a trust-building practice rather than a simple awareness tool. Research Limitations/Future Research: The propositions require empirical testing in diverse cultural and institutional settings. Future studies might assess platform-specific effects or compare nonprofit and for-profit hospital communication.

detail.abstract:
Background. Businesses are increasingly discovered through generative artificial intelligence (AI) search systems such as ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, Google Gemini, and Google AI Overviews. The off-page signals that drive whether a business appears in those answers are not well characterised, and prior work has typically aggregated outcomes across models, masking model-specific behaviour.
Methods. We audited 2,729 businesses across 14 verticals and four metropolitan markets (Los Angeles, New York, Chicago, Sydney). Each business was probed with approximately 95 intent-based prompts across each of five AI systems (ChatGPT GPT-4o, Claude Sonnet, Perplexity sonar-pro, Gemini 2.5-flash, and Google AI Overview via SerpApi), yielding 266,844 paired (business, model, prompt) observations. Each business was enriched with Domain Authority (Moz), organic-traffic and keyword metrics (SpyFu), on-page signals from a direct HTTP crawl (schema, FAQ, indexed pages, blog count, llms.txt), and twelve off-page presence indicators (Reddit, Quora, YouTube, LinkedIn, Wikipedia, Crunchbase, BBB, Yelp, Trustpilot, G2, Capterra, Google Business). We computed Pearson correlations (raw, log-transformed, and Spearman), partial correlations via OLS residualisation, an L2-regularised logistic regression with multicollinearity pruning by variance inflation factor, 95% bootstrap confidence intervals (5,000 resamples), and Benjamini–Hochberg false-discovery-rate (FDR) correction at q = 0.05.
Results. 69.5% of audited businesses (95% CI [67.8%, 71.2%]) were not mentioned by any of the five AI systems; only 1.5% (95% CI [1.06%, 1.98%]) were mentioned by all five. The most novel finding is modelspecific: in per-model strict-isolation analyses (each model treated as a separate binary outcome, with nine controls including Domain Authority and SpyFu metrics), off-page signals including Reddit and Quora mention counts, Wikipedia presence, LinkedIn company pages, and BBB / Yelp / Trustpilot directory presence had small but robust positive partial correlations with mention probability in Claude (partial r up to +0.219), ChatGPT, and Perplexity, but were not significantly associated with mention probability in Gemini or Google AI Overviews. Of 60 model-by-predictor cells, 34 survived BH-FDR at q < 0.05. In paired within-response analyses, businesses whose URL was cited as a source in a Perplexity response were 6.03× more likely to also be mentioned in that response (95% CI [5.62, 6.46]); the corresponding lift for Google AI Overview was 6.64× (95% CI [2.48, 11.30]). Domain Authority, the headline predictor in earlier reporting, had a raw Pearson r of 0.337 but its multivariate logisticregression coefficient confidence interval crossed zero (standardised β = +0.139, 95% CI [−0.031, +0.316]).
Conclusion. Off-page presence is statistically associated with AI mention probability for three of five major generative AI systems, with effect sizes that are small per individual signal (partial r ≈ 0.10–0.22) but consistent across signals. The composite outcome used in earlier reporting averages over models that do and do not respond to off-page signals and consequently understates this relationship. A preregistered controlled trial is planned to test causal magnitude. The dataset and analysis approach are released openly to enable replication.

detail.abstract: Consumer fraud is commonly classified by legal categories, delivery channels, or victim characteristics, but these approaches provide limited insight into the behavioral processes that lead to compliance. This paper proposes the Gain-Exchange-Loss (GEL) multistage framework, which models fraud as a sequential process from exposure to engagement, compliance, and loss realization and classifies interactions by decision environment. Gain-seeking, exchange, and loss-avoidance environments induce distinct cognitive conditions in which deliberation is biased, constrained, or suppressed. The framework integrates insights from behavioral, information, and criminological perspectives and shows that commonly identified factors, including trust, financial literacy, and social connectedness, operate as context-dependent mechanisms rather than fixed predictors of vulnerability. It also highlights dynamic shifts in decision environments and distinguishes stage-specific behavioral responses. By organizing fraud around decision environments and progression across stages, the framework provides a unified account of observed patterns and identifies targeted points for intervention.

title: The Performative Exit: Dissent, Continued Usage, and Institutional Instability in Nigerian Fintech

detail.title: The Performative Exit: Dissent, Continued Usage, and Institutional Instability in Nigerian Fintech
detail.abstract:
Consumer behaviour theory has long assumed that dissatisfied consumers choose between exit and voice. This paper challenges that assumption. Drawing on Hirschman's (1970) exit-voice-loyalty framework, Fournier's (1998) brand relationship typology, and Japutra, Ekinci, and Simkin's (2018) work on brand attachment and negative consumer behaviours, this paper proposes the Performative Exit — a fourth consumer response to brand dissatisfaction in which consumers publicly signal brand withdrawal while privately maintaining continued usage, as a sustained and rational response to markets where full exit is structurally unavailable.

In markets where institutions fail chronically and formal redress is inadequate, consumers construct their own accountability systems. They stay because they must. They complain publicly because it costs nothing and sometimes produces change. The Performative Exit names this pattern, theorises its conditions and mechanisms, and proposes an empirical research agenda for its investigation.

The argument is grounded in the Nigerian digital financial services market, where 320 million active bank accounts are held by approximately 66 million unique individuals, 40.7% of surveyed adults hold at least three accounts simultaneously, and consumer complaints to formal regulatory channels rose 143% year-on-year in 2025, while account numbers continued to grow. In this market, no single provider is reliable enough to anchor exclusive loyalty, no single alternative is sufficient to enable complete exit, and social media platforms have become the primary arena of institutional accountability pressure precisely because formal redress mechanisms have failed to fill that role.

detail.abstract:
Canada's Big Six banks calculate prepayment penalties on fixed-rate mortgages using the Discounted Interest Rate Differential (IRD) method. Borrowers and most brokers focus on the negotiated contract rate. But under the Discounted IRD formula, that contract rate drops out of the penalty calculation entirely.

The math is simple. The effective penalty spread reduces to S = R_P1 - R_P2: the difference between the posted rate at origination and the posted rate at breakage. The client's actual contract rate does not appear. Borrowers think their negotiated discount protects them. It does not. The real driver is a posted-rate benchmark they never see.

The analysis covers Canadian compounding mechanics, refinancing break-even analysis, trigger rates, interpolation effects, and includes an illustrative penalty matrix using Big Six pricing. Small differences in original posted rates can cost borrowers thousands of dollars.

Practical takeaway: borrowers and brokers must evaluate exit costs, not just the headline rate. The paper includes specific questions borrowers should ask before signing any mortgage agreement, plus a proposed standardized disclosure box for regulators.

title: Characterizing Heterogeneous Treatment Effects Using a Hierarchical Bayesian Synthetic Control Model

detail.title: Characterizing Heterogeneous Treatment Effects Using a Hierarchical Bayesian Synthetic Control Model
detail.abstract: Heterogeneity in response to marketing actions is central to marketing theory and practice, yet most quasi-experimental panel methods focus on estimating average treatment effects and examine heterogeneity only through interaction terms or subgroup analyses. We develop a hierarchical Bayesian synthetic control (HBSC) model that integrates causal identification with structured modeling of heterogeneous treatment effects. Building on Bayesian synthetic control methods, the model estimates a treatment effect for each treated unit while simultaneously modeling how these effects vary as a function of observable covariates, enabling formal inference on the determinants of heterogeneity. Simulation studies demonstrate that the proposed approach recovers heterogeneous treatment effects and provides an interpretable characterization of cross-unit differences in treatment effects. We illustrate the method using an application examining the effects of U.S. state-level blockchain legislation on firm valuation, revealing substantial heterogeneity that would be obscured by conventional average-effect approaches.

detail.abstract: This paper introduces the Human Atrophy Index (HAI), a synthetic indicator designed to measure the decline of autonomous human capabilities as a function of technological progress. While classical economic theory interprets innovation as a driver of productivity growth, this study highlights a critical side effect: the erosion of raw human capital. Through the formalisation of 'Functional Delegation', the paper demonstrates how technological advancement shifts value from the individual to the underlying infrastructure, increasing systemic fragility in the event of technological disruption. The model provides a quantitative framework to evaluate the trade-off between efficiency gains and the loss of human autonomy.

detail.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in software engineering, yet most deployments treat them primarily as code-generation instruments. This paper argues that, in high-stakes production systems, the more defensible role is not authorial but institutional: the model should operate as a controlled auditor that reads an authoritative design document, inspects implementation and runtime evidence, and produces bounded verdicts without modifying the system under examination. We introduce the Authority-Driven Development Model (ADDM), a prompt engineering framework for governing long multi-session development work through a fixed design authority, a no-speculation constraint, an evidence taxonomy, established facts, and controlled verdict vocabulary. We identify five structural problems in informal LLM-assisted development-specification drift, plausibility-correctness conflation, session continuity failure, epistemic deference, and auditability loss-and present ADDM as an architectural response to each. The framework is evaluated through a case study involving the construction and audit of a Rust-based automated execution system for fully-collateralised binary prediction markets. The case demonstrates that ADDM can produce reproducible, evidence-grounded milestones that informal conversational development cannot reliably supply. The contribution is both methodological and institutional: prompt engineering is treated not as a usability technique, but as a procedural governance layer for human-AI collaboration in production-grade systems.

title: Data Decay in AI-Driven Marketing: Strategic Mimicry, Aggregation Failure, and Platform Countermeasures

detail.title: Data Decay in AI-Driven Marketing: Strategic Mimicry, Aggregation Failure, and Platform Countermeasures
detail.abstract: Marketing strategy treats behavioral data as a strategic asset that appreciates with scale. We show that this premise can invert when consumer-deployed AI agents adapt strategically to platform classifiers. In a dynamic model of strategic mimicry, accumulated behavioral traces depreciate, depreciation accelerates in AI-agent share, and data can reach a full-mimicry region in which behavioral targeting loses informational value. The platform's optimal response shifts across admission control, data provenance, and accelerated retraining as AI-agent share rises. Calibrating the model on 110,326 transactions from a major Chinese ticketing platform, a pre-rollout machine-speed trace proxy implies 59% data-value erosion (USD 1.6-4.9 million per year), while mandatory identity provenance reduces proxy-calibrated erosion to 16% (USD 0.1-0.4 million). The framework extends marketing's strategic-asset tradition to AI-mediated exchange and gives managers, regulators, and scholars a decision rule for protecting data value.

detail.abstract: The deployment of multi-provider artificial intelligence verification systems in professional contexts creates a novel class of privacy risk that existing AI architectures do not adequately address. When a verification system submits a single user query simultaneously to multiple third-party AI inference engine providers, each submission is a separate data transmission to a separate legal entity, potentially across multiple jurisdictions with different data protection regimes. For professional users including solicitors, compliance officers, financial advisers, and healthcare professionals, who are subject to statutory and professional conduct obligations constraining the disclosure of client information to third parties, this cumulative multi-provider exposure creates a risk of inadvertent breach of confidentiality obligations that is qualitatively different from the risks arising in single-provider AI deployment. This paper presents a privacy-preserving architecture implemented in the TrustAI platform, protected by UK patent application GB2611340.7 filed 14 May 2026, that addresses this risk class through five technical mechanisms. First, user-scoped vector memory isolation enforced at the storage abstraction layer, making cross-user data access architecturally impossible rather than merely programmatically prohibited. Second, substitution-based query anonymisation applied before all external provider submissions, replacing personally identifiable entities with generic semantic placeholders that preserve the query structure necessary for AI response generation. Third, a plan-aware data governance engine applying differentiated data handling policies based on user subscription tier, providing professional-tier users with complete exclusion from retrieval caches and ephemeral session memory retention. Fourth, an ephemeral processing controller managing query content lifecycle with configurable auto-purge schedules. Fifth, a data flow audit logger providing evidentiary compliance documentation without retaining query content. We analyse the legal and regulatory framework applicable to multi-provider AI query architectures under the UK General Data Protection Regulation, the Solicitors Regulation Authority Code of Conduct 2019, the Financial Conduct Authority Senior Managers and Certification Regime, and the legal professional privilege doctrine of English law. We evaluate the architecture against applicable data protection principles and propose a set of design principles for privacy-preserving professional AI deployment that generalise beyond the TrustAI implementation.

detail.title: Personalization, Data Portability and Competitive Dynamics

publicationDetails.detailsText: Boston University and National University of Singapore Research Paper

detail.abstract: We study data portability in a model of dynamic price competition where product quality improves for each customer as personal data accumulates with usage. This can reflect AI-driven personalization based on customer data or customers embedding their own data into the firm's product through usage. We show that when consumers are forward looking and firms can personalize their prices, each firm does best by offering data portability so that its customers can freely take their data to a rival. By contrast, when consumers are myopic, firms no longer always benefit by offering portability, and there are equilibria where neither firm offers data portability. A data portability mandate is therefore redundant when consumers are forward looking, but becomes potentially relevant when consumers are myopic. However, with myopic consumers, a data portability mandate can also cause a complete market breakdown if consumers' initial willingness to pay for firms' products is below cost. We extend these results to a setting without personalized prices.

title: A Study on Multimodal Product Understanding and Assembly Guidance Optimization in e-commerce for Complex Consumer Goods
affiliations: NB Brother Corp, Vernon

detail.title: A Study on Multimodal Product Understanding and Assembly Guidance Optimization in e-commerce for Complex Consumer Goods
detail.abstract: This research deals with the common problems of "not knowing the product before buying and assembling after buying" in the context of online sales of complex consumer products. A multimodal product understanding and assembly guidance optimization approach is proposed to address the information gap between product understanding, feature recognition and assembly execution. The research focuses on consumer products, such as bicycles, which are characterized by multiple components, significant parameters, and reliance on user self-assembly. This scenario is in close agreement with the applicant's actual experience in designing product display images, functional annotations, and installation instructions.Methodologically, the research uses CLIP for the semantic alignment of product images and text, BLIP-2 for the completion of text description and step consistency verification, and for the extraction of key structure visual characteristics. Additionally, a Transformer model encodes product parameter descriptions, component hierarchies, and assembly sequence information.On the basis of this framework, we construct a model of product understanding and a prediction model of assembly task. The User Behavior Analysis includes funnel analysis and Cognitive Load Stratification Assessment, and A/B Test is used to compare the performance of a conventional product page with an optimized solution at the time of purchasing decision-making and assembly execution. The experimental data include 52 product models, 6480 product page interaction records, 1,940 assembly task data points, and 14 months after sales service records.The results show that the optimized solution can increase the precision of product feature comprehension by 33.8%, the average time of assembly task is reduced by 26.9%, and the number of post-sales queries is reduced by 35.7%, and the relevant return request is reduced by 18.4%. Further results show that the problem of semantic mismatch between text and image has been reduced by over 40% with CLIP and BLIP-2. Research shows that the display system for complex consumer products should not be restricted to static visual presentation, but should serve as a digital information infrastructure that integrates product recognition, task orientation and after-sales support. This study is of practical importance to increase the transparency of electronic commerce for complex products, to reduce the risk of false tracking and misassembly, and to optimize the consumer experience.

title: Characteristics of game streaming: A scoping review of social live streaming service features and their involvement with game streaming users
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Nottingham Trent University - Department of Psychology and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Characteristics of game streaming: A scoping review of social live streaming service features and their involvement with game streaming users
detail.abstract: While gaming is the most popular entertainment industry in the world, social networking sites (SNSs) with social live streaming services (SLSSs) grew markedly before, during, and after the COVID-19 pandemic. However, little is known regarding the relationship between game-streaming characteristics (i.e., structural) and game-streaming attitudes and behaviors. Therefore, a review of the structural characteristics of SLSS (e.g., Twitch, YouTube) platforms was conducted adhering to PRISMA guidelines. The included research papers (N = 12) identified characteristics based on similar operational definitions and theoretical frameworks about SLSS features and their function. Results showed that structural characteristics (i.e., communication mediums, social affirmations and validations, third-party tools) found on SNSs with SLSSs appear to influence user engagement. The present review contributes to understanding the relationship between machine-design and SLSS user behaviors and identifying and organizing examples of structural characteristics.

detail.abstract: Saudi Arabia's digital transformation agenda has produced a regulatory environment that is comprehensive in its ambition but uneven in its operational specificity when applied to artificial intelligence and big data workloads. Public-sector enterprises in the Kingdom are deploying AI capabilities at scale, embedding machine learning into enterprise resource planning processes, integrating cloud-native data platforms with SAP and adjacent systems, and increasingly evaluating generative AI for content generation, summarization, and process automation. Each of these deployments operates within a regulatory perimeter defined by the Saudi Data and AI Authority, the National Cybersecurity Authority, and the Communications and Space Technology Commission, and each raises governance questions that the current instruments address at the level of principle but not at the level of operational implementation. This paper investigates how five governance domains central to enterprise AI and big data deployments, namely data lineage and classification, model lifecycle governance, integration trust and identity, observability and audit-readiness, and ethics operationalization, are addressed by the principal Saudi regulatory instruments: the National Strategy for Data and AI, the Personal Data Protection Law, the SDAIA AI Ethics Principles, the Cloud Computing Regulatory Framework, and the Essential and Cloud Cybersecurity Controls. The study uses a systematic document analysis methodology, cross-referencing the Saudi instruments against the NIST AI Risk Management Framework and against published technical guidance from SAP Business Technology Platform and Amazon Web Services. Across the five domains, the study finds that regulatory coverage is coherent at the policy level but leaves significant operational implementation gaps, particularly for model lifecycle governance, AI-derived data classification, and the integrated audit-readiness requirement that emerges from combining NCA logging obligations with SDAIA explicability principles. The study also examines generative AI compliance considerations, including prompt governance, hallucination risk, and cross-border model placement, finding that current instruments do not yet address these concerns with sufficient specificity for enterprise implementation. The findings contribute to an understanding of how regulated public-sector organizations can structure compliant AI and big data programmes while the regulatory framework continues to mature.

title: Nurses as Operational Shock Absorbers: A RUISA®-Based Conceptual Analysis of Hidden Instability in Healthcare Systems
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Nurses as Operational Shock Absorbers: A RUISA®-Based Conceptual Analysis of Hidden Instability in Healthcare Systems

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no known personal or financial relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This work is conceptual in nature and did not involve human participants, patient data, identifiable clinical records, or institutional review board approval.

detail.abstract:
Healthcare systems often appear stable through visible indicators such as completed shifts, maintained patient flow, submitted reports, bed movement, and dashboard performance. However, visible stability may not fully capture the hidden adaptive work performed by front-line nurses. This conceptual paper uses RUISA, an author-developed operational coherence framework, to examine nurses as operational shock absorbers within complex healthcare systems.

The paper argues that nurses frequently absorb operational strain created by delayed information, unclear ownership, fragmented communication, staffing pressure, documentation burden, blocked patient movement, and disconnected workflows. While this absorption may protect continuity and patient care in the short term, repeated dependence on nursing strain can conceal system defects and delay structural correction.

Using a RUISA-based interpretation, the paper distinguishes between healthy front-line resilience and unmanaged operational instability transferred to the bedside. It proposes that healthcare leaders should move beyond asking whether work was completed and instead examine how much avoidable pressure was absorbed by nurses for the work to appear complete.

The paper frames nursing workarounds not as individual failure, but as signals of deeper system incoherence when they become repetitive, normalized, and necessary for daily function. From this perspective, true operational stability is not the absence of visible failure, but the early visibility of pressure, clear ownership, connected information, timely action, and reduced unnecessary burden on front-line staff.

The paper contributes a RUISA-based conceptual language for identifying hidden operational strain before it becomes burnout, error, delay, or operational collapse.

title: Constructibility Monitoring and Early Collapse Detection in Neural Learning Systems A Margin-Based Early Warning Framework for Accuracy Failure under Corruption and Resource Constraints
affiliations: Azerbaijan Technical University and

detail.title: Constructibility Monitoring and Early Collapse Detection in Neural Learning Systems A Margin-Based Early Warning Framework for Accuracy Failure under Corruption and Resource Constraints
detail.abstract: Paper 1 [1] established that learning collapse under synthetic corruption follows a sharp boundary governed by a power-law eective capacity constraint L(S) = C β n γ /H α. The boundary location is predictable; its approach is not monitored. This paper introduces the Constructibility Margin M(t) = log L(S)(t)-log R(S)(t) as a real-time early warning signal. We prove that M(t) is monotone decreasing before collapse (Theorem 4.1), establish a lead-time lower bound ∆t ≥ M 0 /| Ṁ| (Theorem 4.3), and derive a false alarm rate bound under stable operating conditions (Proposition 4.7). Empirically, across the same three transformer architectures (DistilBERT, BERT-base, RoBERTa-large) and two benchmarks (IMDb, SST-2), M(t) crosses a warning threshold with mean lead time ∆t = 4.2 ± 1.1 corruption steps before accuracy collapse, achieving detection AUC = 0.91 ± 0.03 compared to loss-based detection AUC = 0.71 ± 0.05 and variance-based AUC = 0.74 ± 0.04.

title: The Proxy Trap:  Why AI Systems Optimize What Is Measurable Instead of What Matters

detail.title: The Proxy Trap:  Why AI Systems Optimize What Is Measurable Instead of What Matters

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest related to this research.
declarations.ethicsApproval: No human participants or patient data were involved in this research.
declarations.funderStatement: This research was independently conducted and self-funded by the author.

detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence systems require measurable objectives in order to optimize performance. Yet many of the outcomes organizations actually seek-trust, long-term value creation, customer satisfaction, institutional resilience, or strategic advantage-are difficult to measure directly. As a result, organizations frequently substitute proxy metrics that are easier to quantify and operationalize. Over time, AI systems optimize these measurable surrogates with increasing efficiency, often causing the proxy itself to become detached from the original economic or strategic objective. This paper defines this phenomenon as the Proxy Trap: a condition in which optimization systems improve measurable indicators while underlying economic outcomes stagnate or deteriorate. The paper argues that proxy distortion is not an isolated technical issue but a structural characteristic of learning systems operating under optimization pressure. Using the example of engagement optimization in large-scale social media recommendation systems, the paper demonstrates how metric optimization can diverge from institutional intent, creating hidden strategic risk despite improving operational performance. The paper concludes that the central challenge in AI strategy is not merely building systems that optimize efficiently, but ensuring that optimization remains aligned with enduring economic objectives over time.

detail.abstract: Employing large language models to analyze official documents, we construct a comprehensive record of daily changes in de jure restrictions on cross-border flows worldwide since the 1950s. Our analysis uncovers the wide array of instruments used to regulate cross-border financial flows over the past seven decades, leveraging the fine granularity of the new measures to characterize cross-country and time-series variation across eight categories of restrictions —- distinguishing by flow, direction, instrument type, intensity, and overall policy stance. We exploit the high frequency nature of the new data to document novel patterns in the use of these restrictions, as well as their relationship to crises and political economy determinants.

title: The Central Bank’s Dilemma
affiliations: University of British Columbia (UBC) - Vancouver School of Economics,  and

detail.title: The Central Bank’s Dilemma

publicationDetails.journalName: International Monetary Fund (IMF) Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: When countries are hit by supply shocks, central banks often face the dilemma of either looking through such shocks or reacting to them to ensure that inflation expectations remain anchored. In this paper, we propose a tractable framework to capture this dilemma and explore optimal policy under various assumptions on how agents form their expectations and the sophistication with which those expectations account for the central bank’s announced policies. While our analysis covers a wide range of potential specifications, our baseline results focus on level-k thinking (LKT) – a form of bounded rationality that enjoys significant support in the experimental literature and encompasses both adaptive expectations (AE) and rational expectations (RE) as special cases. Nonetheless, we show that the optimal policy under LKT is qualitatively very different from its analogues under AE and RE, exhibiting abrupt pivots in the policy stance. In particular, it is optimal for the central bank to initially look through supply shocks until a threshold is reached, then pivot discontinuously to a more hawkish anti-inflationary stance. We find that such pivots can, if optimally executed, be compatible with soft landings in the sense that most (or even all) of the reduction in inflation occurs through re-anchoring of expectations rather than economic slack. We also discuss risks and why policy errors in terms of tightening too late or too slowly can be especially costly in such an environment.

The update incorporates new episodes, while maintaining the definition established in previous editions, which emphasizes both significant signs of financial distress and substantial policy interventions. The update integrates textual tools to screen potential candidates that are then further scrutinized to confirm if our definition is met. The database includes information on banking crises episodes during 1970-2025, including starting dates, policy responses, fiscal costs, and output losses. It offers a comprehensive tool for assessing cross-country vulnerabilities and policies to resolve banking crises.

detail.title: Mind the Gaps

publicationDetails.journalName: International Monetary Fund (IMF) Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: This paper analyzes trade patterns across the Caribbean Community (CARICOM)—15 Caribbean countries—and makes three main contributions. First, it provides a unified empirical assessment of Caribbean external connectivity by jointly analyzing goods trade, tourism flows, and cross-border banking linkages within a consistent gravity-model framework. Second, it presents new evidence on the role of physical connectivity—shipping and air transport—in shaping both import source concentration and tourism inflows, drawing on granular bilateral trade, tourism, and flight capacity data. Third, it shows that, while financial connectivity matters in a global context, it is not the primary binding constraint for Caribbean economies; instead, limited physical connectivity emerges as the more decisive factor shaping trade patterns and external vulnerabilities.

detail.title: When Policy Bites

detail.abstract: We document the state-dependence of monetary policy transmission to output and core consumer prices in a sample of eleven large inflation-targeting emerging markets along three cyclical dimensions: the business cycle position, the monetary policy stance, and the level of trend inflation. We show that monetary policy has strong effects on output during recessions and after a period of loose monetary policy, but little to no impact during expansions or when monetary policy has been tight. In contrast, the response of prices is muted regardless of business cycle position or monetary policy stance. Transmission also depends on trend inflation: when trend inflation is low, monetary policy has a stronger impact on output and a weaker effect on prices, whereas a high-inflation environment dampens the output response and amplifies price adjustments. These findings are broadly consistent with the presence of financial frictions in the form of occasionally binding borrowing constraints, endogenous frequency of price adjustments, loss aversion preferences, and a convex Phillips Curve.
